cloudlandsdev 2026/10/25 17:27
Update: Did not expect the amount of traffic! Every time I scale the VPS, y'all immediately blow through the extra compute. Should be up again, hopefully will be more stable once this drops off the front page.

Any attempt at logging so I can make a blog about the successful solve is gonna be best effort, don't have disk capacity to keep up with the traffic (at peak it was rotating every 12 min...). If you win the challenge, write-ups are definitely welcome.

For those who are saying that the nginx config is unfairly difficult, intention was just to replicate a fairly normal config that was more realistic than you'd get in a lab environment. If we get to 24 hr+ with no solves I'll see about making it easier. In the meantime, seems like you can perhaps mitigate PHP2Shell with the right nginx config, so that's pretty neat!

LiveOverflow 2026/10/26 02:05
OP confirmed that the server was initially serving only an index.html. In that configuration, the vulnerable code path is never reached — it requires a .php file.

OP added php-version.php roughly 18–19 hours into the experiment (I'm not sure of the exact timing), so that period should be subtracted from the publicly displayed challenge duration.

Based on my external fingerprinting, I now believe the setup should actually be exploitable!

However, the server is being absolutely hammered with requests and crashes. Making it significantly harder to pull off. This is imo still an unrealistic target. If you are not taking the top 1% PHP websites, then they will have long periods (1 minute) of no traffic.

If someone manages to pull off a working exploit under these conditions, that would be crazy to me.

NorwegianDude 2026/10/26 11:08
This was presented as a normal setup of PHP, but in reality was something completely different. Nobody runs PHP like this. This used the dev server in PHP and proxied requests from nginx to the php http dev server. Literally the first thing in the php docs about the dev server is:

"Warning This web server is designed to aid application development. It may also be useful for testing purposes or for application demonstrations that are run in controlled environments. It is not intended to be a full-featured web server. It should not be used on a public network."

It's also singel threaded and very slow, so that explains why the site was so damn unusable.

It's a shame, as a realistic setup would be much more informative.
